Subject: Proposal - Dedicated GPU tranche schedule and multi-year prepay structure

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great conversation on Calypso's inference profile and the spike patterns you see at quarter boundaries. Per our ask, attached is a draft pricing matrix that maps a 24-month commitment to a three-tranche ramp (small alpha pool -> mid production -> full steady state).

High-level summary:
- 24-month term with annual prepay option (yr1 prepaid; yr2 prepaid at 50% with balance amortized)
- Tranche delivery: Month 0 (10% of committed GPUs), Month 6 (50%), Month 12 (100%)
- Term discount ladder: 15% flat list for full upfront; 10% for standard annual prepay; additional 3% for multi-year renewal guarantee

Questions for you:
1) Is the Month 6 acceleration acceptable for your initial production needs, or do you need an earlier mid-ramp (e.g., Month 3)?
2) Any mandatory language your procurement team requires for amortization or breakage credits if you scale down in year 2?

I attached pricing_matrix_v4.xlsx for the numeric examples. If this aligns, we can produce a clean redline of the MSA and amortization schedule for your procurement review.

Would you like to sync next week to walk through the tranche economics? I can bring our finance lead (Marissa) if you want line-item modeling.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0122

Attachment: pricing_matrix_v4.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72 KB)
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@calypso.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal - Dedicated GPU tranche schedule and multi-year prepay structure

Jordan — thanks for the file and summary. A few notes from our side after an initial review:

- The tranche cadence looks promising. We prefer an earlier mid-step (Month 3) because our product team plans a beta in Q2 that will need more capacity than the Month 6 window you proposed.
- Procurement flagged the amortization language — they typically want a clause that allows a one-time downward adjustment at the 12-month mark with a 60-day notice, subject to a 10% breakage fee.
- For discounts: our CFO has mandated that any >12% effective discount requires board notification. We would prefer structuring the economics so headline discount appears as a timing incentive (prepay) rather than a contractual multi-year price concession.

I'm looping Dan (procurement) to keep this on their radar. We're keen to move quickly but need to ensure the ramp timing and the breakage mechanism are palatable.

Can your team rerun the numbers with a Month 3 mid-ramp (10% -> 40% -> 100%) and an amortization option that reflects the 12-month adjustment window + 10% fee?

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Platform Ops, Calypso Analytics
emily.cho@calypso.ai

Emily — appreciate the clarity. Lauren / Marissa — tagging you for modeling input.

Quick internal notes:
- We can shift mid-ramp to Month 3 (10% -> 40% -> 100%) with modest pricing impact; it increases near-term consumption exposure and slightly reduces effective discount unless fully prepaid.
- Procurement request (12-mo adjustment + 10% breakage) is reasonable as a commercial concession but we'll want to limit it to a single exercise during the term to avoid churn risk.
- Finance will need to see amortization schedule options: (A) full upfront prepay; (B) year1 full prepay + year2 50% prepay + amortized balance; (C) equal annual prepay.

Marissa — can you produce a table with those three amortization scenarios and the effective per-GPU-month rate?

Jordan

Subject: Re: Proposal - Dedicated GPU tranche schedule and multi-year prepay structure (amortization scenarios)

Attaching amortization_schedule_qtr_tranches.xlsx — three scenarios modeled at the per-GPU-month level. Top-line notes:

- Option A (full upfront prepay): lowest effective unit cost (~18% lower than list) and simplest accounting.
- Option B (Yr1 full prepay, Yr2 50% prepay + amortize): strikes balance; effective discount ~12% depending on acceleration timing.
- Option C (equal annual prepay): highest flexibility for customer, smallest headline discount (~8%).

Impact of moving mid-ramp to Month 3: increases near-term cash burn for Redwoods but we can preserve Option B pricing by slightly shortening the amortization window (move more of yr2 into prepaid portion).

I also drafted suggested contract language for a single 12-month adjustment with a 10% breakage fee and explicit cap on downward capacity adjustments (max 30% of committed GPUs). Sending redline separately once Jordan confirms direction.

-Marissa
Finance, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Lauren — attaching our procurement team's redlined MSA for your legal review. Key asks: 1) explicit audit rights and subprocessor list; 2) a 45-day termination for convenience with partial pro-rata credit tied to remaining committed capacity; 3) a cap on liability tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months.

We appreciate the amortization scenarios from Marissa. Our CFO still wants the headline discount to read as a timing benefit, not a guaranteed price decline in year 2. Please review the attached redlined_msa_calypso.pdf and advise if Redwood can accept the breakage clause + 45-day termination + liability cap language.

- Chosen payment structure: Option B (Yr1 full prepay, Yr2 50% prepay + amortized balance) — preserves effective discount at ~12% without making the discount a contractual recurring price cut.
